title: Batched calibration and A/B orchestration for reranking evaluations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Reranking endpoint quality regressions are currently detected too late and with noisy signals. We lack a standardized, repeatable pipeline that computes per-customer NDCG and MRR over their prompt sets, performs statistical comparisons across model variants, and ties those signals to canary/A-B traffic routing.

Goal: Ship an automated batched evaluation and calibration pipeline that (1) computes daily NDCG/MRR with confidence intervals for each customer promptset, (2) supports stratified sampling and weighted metrics to handle skewed query distributions, (3) exposes an evaluation dashboard and gating rules for rollouts, and (4) surfaces latency/throughput tradeoffs alongside quality so Product/SEs can choose model-variant policies.

Scope: offline batched evaluation job + lightweight online instrumentation for sampled traffic, dashboards in Console, gating webhooks for rollout orchestration. Exclude full labeling UIs (we will integrate existing labeling service later).
acceptance_criteria: Daily batch job computes per-customer NDCG@k (k=1,5,10) and MRR with 95% bootstrap CIs and stores results in metrics table
Dashboard tile in Console listing top-10 regressions by absolute NDCG drop and latency delta
A/B orchestration accepts pass/fail rule based on thresholded delta with configurable sample size and automatically promotes/rolls-back variant via rollout API
Online sampling hook emits per-request eval events (golden label vs. model rank) in <100ms added latency and under feature flag
Integration tests for the batched pipeline, statistical test utils, and end-to-end gating flow (mock rollout)
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket after review with PM and product analytics. Initial design doc linked. Need engineering estimates for bootstrapping variance calculations.

2026-02-25 Luca Martín: Spike completed — implemented sample harness that replays production traffic into local rerank binary. Found that naive pooling across customers inflates NDCG variance due to heavy users. Proposal: per-customer stratified bootstrap and exponential smoothing for baseline drift.
2026-02-28 Review (PM): Ashwin Patel requested that we include latency percentiles alongside quality metrics on the same row in the dashboard so product managers can see tradeoffs at a glance.
2026-03-02 Design feedback: Priya Rao suggested a compact sparkline view per customer + expand to full cohort history. We will start with top-issue customers and expose API for custom queries.

2026-03-04 Infra note: Using existing batch infra (Airflow -> Dataflow) to run the evaluation jobs. Initial cost estimate: +0.6 compute units/day for full-cust daily job; we will add downsampling config for very large customers to keep costs predictable. Linked PR to configure pipeline: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-eval/pull/612

2026-03-05 Luca Martín: Implemented metric exporter and unit tests for bootstrap CI computation. End-to-end test against synthetic customer promptset shows correct detection of a simulated 4% NDCG drop with p<0.01. Preparing dashboard wireframe and rollout webhook prototype.
implementation_notes: Metric computation: use stratified bootstrap (per-customer) + block bootstrap for temporal correlation in long-running queries
Sampling: deterministic reservoir sampling for reproducible offline runs; reservoir size default 10k per-customer with configurable cap
Storage: results written to metrics-store (time-series table) with schema: customer_id, model_variant, date, ndcg@1, ndcg@5, ndcg@10, mrr, latency_p50, latency_p95, ci_lower, ci_upper
Rollout gating: small control library that accepts metric diffs and sample sizes, performs two-sided tests and returns PASS/FAIL; integrates with rollout-api for canary change
Online hook: lightweight evaluator that only runs for sampled requests and posts events to eval-queue (async) to avoid adding tail latency
Backfill plan: initial backfill for last 30 days using nightly job; mark early dates as estimated until we can re-run with ground-truth sets
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Small promptsets yield noisy estimates -> Mitigation: require minimum effective sample size for gating and use smoothed baselines
Risk: Cost of full per-customer daily runs for very large customers -> Mitigation: adaptive downsampling and configurable retention window
Risk: Latency instrumentation may leak PII -> Mitigation: strip request payloads and only store hashed prompt ids and ranks
Risk: False positives from multiple comparisons across customers -> Mitigation: FDR correction applied for alerting and dashboard ranking
